finding.title: Hoist EmptyLoginScreen's getAllAccounts() future out of build()
finding.why: future: is evaluated fresh on every rebuild of EmptyLoginScreen (theme change, locale change, any ancestor rebuild), so FutureBuilder restarts from its loading/no-data state each time, re-querying the device registry and making the account-switch icon flicker/disappear-and-reappear on unrelated rebuilds instead of staying stable.
finding.recommendation: Move the Future into a @riverpod FutureProvider (e.g. allDeviceAccountsProvider) and ref.watch it, or cache it in a late final in a stateful wrapper.
acceptance_criteria: a widget test that triggers an unrelated rebuild of EmptyLoginScreen asserts getAllAccounts() is called exactly once, not once per rebuild

finding.title: Remove unreachable English-only default parameter values in AppIntroScreen's _IntroPage
finding.why: Both call sites (_buildSubtitleBlock at line 292 and its internal call to _subtitleRich) always pass an explicit talmidChochomLabel: terms.talmidChochom argument, so these English-literal defaults can never actually render -- dead code that also looks like (but isn't reachable as) an AX-2 violation, wasting a reviewer's attention when auditing for hardcoded strings.
finding.recommendation: Make the parameter `required String talmidChochomLabel` (drop the default) so the compiler enforces callers always supply the localized value.
acceptance_criteria: flutter analyze clean after making the parameter required (proves no call site relied on the default)

finding.title: Delete or consolidate the orphaned duplicate features/account/onboarding/domain/validators/auth_validators.dart
finding.why: Two files sharing the same basename define byte-identical bodies for validateEmail/validatePassword/validateDisplayName. A repo-wide grep confirms the features/account/onboarding/ copy has zero importers — it is dead code left over from the account-feature migration that features/onboarding/onboarding.dart's own doc comment describes as in-progress. An agent grepping 'validateEmail' will find both definitions and may edit the dead one, producing a silent no-op — exactly the accretion failure AG-4 exists to prevent.
finding.recommendation: Delete lib/features/account/onboarding/domain/validators/auth_validators.dart. If features/account/onboarding/ is the intended long-term home per the migration note, move (not copy) the real implementation there instead and repoint the 2 importers found in finding 3.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn "features/account/onboarding/domain/validators/auth_validators.dart'" lib/ test/ returns no importers before deletion (already true today)

finding.title: Route features/account/* imports of onboarding validators/screens through the onboarding barrel, not deep paths

evidence.quote: // Import this barrel (features/onboarding/onboarding.dart) from outside this

finding.why: features/onboarding/onboarding.dart is the designated public surface ('Do NOT import deep paths directly') but it is an 8-line stub with zero export statements. Two account-feature screens (both audit HOTSPOT files) have no compliant way to reach auth_validators.dart and instead reach 2-3 directories deep into another feature's domain/ internals. A repo-wide grep shows this same pattern recurring ~26 times across 15 other files reaching into features/onboarding/, so this batch's file is one instance of a feature with an effectively non-functional barrel.
finding.recommendation: Populate features/onboarding/onboarding.dart with real exports (at minimum auth_validators.dart's public surface and whatever of onboarding_screen.dart is legitimately consumed cross-feature) and repoint the 2 importers at the barrel.
acceptance_criteria: Once the check-15/15 fix (paired finding) is in place, `make audit` reports zero cross-feature deep imports into lib/features/onboarding/ from signup_screen.dart and sign_in_screen.dart

finding.title: Fix the always-passing awk comparison in Makefile check 15/15 (no-cross-feature-deep-imports)

evidence.quote: match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print

finding.why: match($0, ...) scans the whole 'path:lineno:content' grep line and matches the FIRST 'features/xxx/' occurrence, which is always inside the file-path prefix — identical to what match($1, ...) already extracted. a[1] and b[1] are therefore always equal and the filter never prints, regardless of which feature is actually imported. Running the exact command directly against the current tree confirms 0 output even though the 18 cross-feature-import lines cited in the paired finding (and ~26 total repo-wide) exist. Rule 2 has had zero real enforcement, even as a warning, since this check was written.
finding.recommendation: Match the import path portion only (e.g. split on the literal single-quote around the package path before matching, or grep the content field explicitly by re-slicing on the first two colons). Add a fixture case to the audit's own coverage so a future edit to this check can't silently break it again.
acceptance_criteria: Running the check-15/15 grep+awk pipeline against a temporary file containing a known deep cross-feature import produces WARN output instead of silently passing
After the fix, `make audit` output for the current tree lists the auth_validators.dart / onboarding_screen.dart cross-feature imports from finding 3
